I present to you all: a visualization I made on the 2nd day of class.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)


url <- 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmzobitz/HNDSDatasets/refs/heads/main/data-raw/unemployment_data.csv'

unemployment_data <- read_csv(file = url)

# Type your response here.
ggplot(data = unemployment_data, aes(
  x = Year, y = unemployment_rate, color = Area_Name
  )) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point() +
  theme_linedraw() +
  labs(
    title = "Twin Cities Unemployment rate trends",
    subtitle = "Data from https://www.ers.usda.gov/",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color = "County"
  )
```

Hurts your eyes, doesn't it? To be fair, I was relearning R at this point, and it had been a year since I had used it (oops...) so... <br>
Let's see how I can make this look better!

Maybe a new splash of color...?
```{r}
plot <- ggplot(data = unemployment_data, aes(
  x = Year, y = unemployment_rate, color = Area_Name
  )) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point() +
  theme_linedraw() +
  labs(
    title = "Twin Cities Unemployment rate trends",
    subtitle = "Data from https://www.ers.usda.gov/",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color = "County"
  )
plot + scale_color_brewer(palette = "paired")
```
Well that certainly isn't confusing at all. Let's try a different graph style this time, along with a new color palette.
(i'm rereading this and i'm realizing that i sound like an LLM, which makes me sad.
although, does that mean i'm losing my humanity, or is an LLM getting better at
mimicking it? questions for later i guess.)

```{r}
library(paletteer)

plot <- ggplot(data = unemployment_data, aes(
  x = Year, y = unemployment_rate, color = Area_Name
  )) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(fill = NA) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  labs(
    title = "Twin Cities Unemployment rate trends",
    subtitle = "Data from https://www.ers.usda.gov/",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color = "County"
  )
plot + scale_color_paletteer_d("fishualize::Chlorurus_spilurus")

```
Now that's more like it!<br>
The color palette is all nice, the graph doesn't look like a heart rate monitor,
and it still gets the message across! It's all I ever wanted!

For the previous one, I was too focused on including the spikes in the graph. The
preservationist in me wanted to keep everything on the graph, which isn't a bad
mentality to have at all! Just not a good mentality for data sometimes, since then
you can end up with the rainbow mess that was the first graph.

Hopefully my future graphs will be better...
